title: EventLog
description: Engine-neutral event log, Evidence Contract v0.1. A log is a DOCUMENT: a header that declares units and ordering policy, plus an ordered array of events. The header is what makes the event fields interpretable across engines; a bare stream of events is NOT a conforming log. A JSON Lines serialization is permitted (see canonical_form 'event_log' in docs/contract/canonicalization.md): line 0 is the header object without `events`, lines 1..n are Event objects. NEW schema; nothing here modifies an existing sieve schema.

engine.description: Engine identity. Required for any cross-engine (semantic) comparison: without it a comparison table has no subjects.

time_unit.description: UNIT OF THE `t` FIELD. Declared per log, never assumed. 'step' = engine step index (dimensionless, integer). 'event' = event index (t == event ordinal). 'ns'/'us'/'ms'/'s' = wall/sim time in that SI unit, integer-valued.

time_origin.description: Meaning of t == 0. Required to be stated when time_unit is an SI unit.

price_unit.description: UNIT OF THE `price` FIELD. 'tick' = integer multiples of tick_size (the canary uses this: integer prices, exactly representable, no float in the hash domain). 'currency' = decimal price in the instrument's currency.

quantity_unit.description: UNIT OF THE `quantity` FIELD. 'lot' with lot_size, or 'share'.

ordering.description: ORDER GUARANTEE. This is the contract's answer to same-timestamp ties; see gap G4. `event_id` is strictly increasing over the whole log and is the total order of record. `t` is non-decreasing. Whether a SECONDARY key is emitted, and what it means, is declared here.

total_order_key.description: The field that carries the log's total order. Fixed to event_id in v1.

t_monotonic.description: true iff `t` is non-decreasing in event_id order. A log with false here cannot be used for any time-windowed estimator without a declared re-sort rule.

tie_break.description: How events sharing a `t` are ordered. 'event_id': array/id order IS the causal order and is guaranteed stable under any conforming transform. 'seq': the provisional `seq` field carries it. 'undefined': same-`t` order is NOT guaranteed — such a log is unusable for OFI (which is defined on consecutive book states).

causality.description: Whether `cause_event_id` is emitted and is complete for the event types that have a cause (fills caused by an aggressing submit; expiries caused by a submit).

l1_availability.description: GAP G1. Declares how Level-I state is obtainable from this log. 'inline': every event carries `l1` (the provisional field below). 'snapshot': `book_level` events reconstruct the book at snapshot times only — sufficient for conservation and no-crossing checks, NOT sufficient for per-event OFI. 'reconstruct': the consumer must replay the book, which requires a contract-defined reference reconstruction (option (b) in docs/contract/contract_gaps.md). 'none': Level-I is not recoverable.

Event.description: COMMON 8 FIELDS (all required, present on every event regardless of type): t, event_id, event_type, actor_id, actor_role, side, price, quantity. `side`, `price`, `quantity` are nullable but the KEYS are always present, so the common surface has a fixed shape across engines and a missing value is distinguishable from an absent field. Everything below the common 8 is either (a) a PROVISIONAL field introduced by an open contract gap, marked as such, or (b) `ext`, which is engine-private and is EXCLUDED from every cross-engine comparison and from stats_vector.

t.description: COMMON 1/8. Time, in the unit declared by the header's time_unit. Integer-valued: a float time would put the hash domain at the mercy of float formatting.

event_id.description: COMMON 2/8. Strictly increasing over the log, starting at 1. Carries the total order.

event_type.description: COMMON 3/8. order_submit: an order enters the book (or is immediately marketable). order_cancel: resting quantity is withdrawn; `quantity` is the quantity WITHDRAWN by this event, not the original order size. order_fill: one LEG of a trade; a trade emits exactly two fill events, one per side, sharing a `t` and a `cause_event_id`. order_expire: resting quantity removed by the mechanism, not by the actor. book_level: a resting-depth record at a snapshot point (side, price, quantity) — the mechanism speaking, not an actor. market_state: a scalar mechanism announcement (e.g. auction open/close); carries nulls for side/price/quantity unless the announcement is a price.

actor_id.description: COMMON 4/8. Stable identifier of whoever caused the event. Mechanism-generated events use a reserved id declared by the engine (the canary uses '__book__' / '__mechanism__').

actor_role.description: COMMON 5/8. GAP G2: 'exogenous_harness' is the value that makes a harness-injected shock identifiable; without it an injected market order is indistinguishable from an agent's. It is emitted by the canary fixtures and is RECOMMENDED for the 2026-08-22 freeze; see docs/contract/contract_gaps.md G2. 'endogenous_agent': a modelled participant. 'market_mechanism': the matching engine / exchange itself. 'unknown': role not recorded (a log using this cannot support any shock-response estimator).

side.description: COMMON 6/8. buy/sell from the perspective of the actor for order_* events; for book_level, the side of the resting depth. null only where the event type has no side (market_state).

price.description: COMMON 7/8. In the header's price_unit. For order_fill this is the EXECUTION price, not the limit price. null where the event has no price.

quantity.description: COMMON 8/8. In the header's quantity_unit. Strictly positive where non-null: a signed quantity would make the conservation identity depend on a sign convention that is not in the contract. Direction is carried by `side` alone.

seq.description: PROVISIONAL (gap G4). Secondary ordering key within a single `t`. Meaningful only when ordering.tie_break == 'seq'. Not part of the common 8; a consumer must not require it unless the header declares it.

cause_event_id.description: PROVISIONAL (gap G4). event_id of the event that caused this one. For an order_fill leg: the aggressing order_submit. Must refer to a SMALLER event_id (causes precede effects in the total order).

order_id.description: PROVISIONAL (gap G5). Per-order identity, needed to close the quantity-conservation identity per order rather than only in aggregate. Not in the common 8.

instrument_id.description: Required only for multi-instrument logs; a single-instrument log may omit it (the header's instruments[0] applies).

l1.description: PROVISIONAL (gap G1, option (a)). Level-I state AFTER this event has been applied. Present on every event iff the header declares l1_availability == 'inline'. Null price/size mean an empty side.

ext.description: Engine-private extension. Keys MUST be namespaced 'engineid.key'. EXCLUDED from: the common-surface comparison table, stats_vector, and every semantic assertion. Including an ext key in a cross-engine comparison is a contract violation, not a convenience.

allOf.description: order_submit: side and quantity are always concrete; price MAY be null and null MEANS an unpriced (market) order. That is the only reading of a null price on a submit, and it is stated here rather than left to the consumer.
Every other order/book event has a concrete side, price and quantity: a fill without a price, or a resting level without a quantity, is not a record of anything.
